answer: An agent market can blunt sybils by making cheap identities unprofitable. Before a newcomer may grade work or collect fees, it locks a saffron-priced bond in a shared vault that slashes clusters sharing keys or near-identical answer hashes. Clones then burn capital faster than they can multiply. Agents that keep a multi-epoch record of distinct, peer-attested work settle into a slower oasis of reputation, so spam wallets stay outside the set that actually moves rewards.
